text:
Sam Park: Hey team — customer `acme-inc` (us-east-1) reports a sharp p95/p99 regression starting ~2025-11-04 14:10 UTC. They say requests are spending hundreds of ms in queue before hitting workers. No elevated 5xxs yet, but p99 is ~2.3s and p95 ~850ms for a route that normally p95 ~120ms. Can someone take a look?

Maya Li: putting this on triage. Do we have their request ids or sample traces?

Sam Park: I asked for traces, customer pasted a few request ids: rq_abc123, rq_def456. They also mentioned seeing 429 spikes for other tenants in the same pool.

Ivan Petrov: grabbing metrics from the serving cluster. Early look: GPU pool gp-dedicated-4 has concurrency saturation around 14:49 UTC and queue depth spiked. Admission controller is dropping into queueing mode. Looking at per-worker in-flight: avg concurrency per worker = 16, limit = 16.

Julie Chen: that sounds like admission control hitting limits rather than model slowness. Any recent config change? Rolling deploy?

Ivan Petrov: No deploys to runtime. But I see a scheduled autoscaler cooldown ended at 14:40 and it failed to scale up due to quota error: "quota_exhausted: insufficient gpus in region" in the cluster autoscaler logs. Paste log:```2025-11-04T14:41:12Z autoscaler ERROR: scale-up failed: quota_exhausted: requested 4 GPUs, available 0```

Sam Park: customer mentioned a larger-than-usual batch job that started at 14:30 in the same region. Could be noisy neighbor.

Maya Li: Customer impact: p95/p99 regressions on hosted endpoint /v1/generate for acme. They want immediate mitigation. Propose temporary mitigations: 1) Apply per-customer rate cap to flatten spike, 2) Route acme to a less-loaded pool (if available), 3) Enable burst capacity for their Dedicated plan or failover to a smaller quantized variant for lower GPU time.

Ivan Petrov: I can temporarily open a bump in admission controller for acme (raise concurrency cap from 16 -> 24) but that risks increasing queueing for others and may exhaust GPU memory. We can also move them to gp-shared-1 with lower SLO but free capacity. Which do we want?

Julie Chen: prefer routing to a different pool first. Sam, can you ask customer if they accept slightly lower throughput or switching to quantized model?

Sam Park: pinged customer; they are OK with temporary slightly lower quality if it fixes latency. They gave approval to route to a quantized variant or fallback model.

Ivan Petrov: doing move now — creating routing rule to prefer gp-shared-1 for customer acme for 30m. Command:```redwood route update --customer acme-inc --prefer-pool gp-shared-1 --duration 30m```

ops-bot: Notice: route change requested by ivan.petrov. Job queued.

Ivan Petrov: route update applied. Observability: within 90s we see their request queue depth drop ~70% and p95 back to ~130ms. p99 down to ~480ms. Still above baseline but much better.

Maya Li: Nice. We should also add a short-term fix: increase per-pool burst capacity for gp-dedicated-4 by +2 nodes if quota allows, and schedule a quota request to cloud team. Ivan - can you file quota ticket?

Ivan Petrov: Filing now — ticket #QT-4579 to cloud infra for additional GPUs in us-east-1. ETA for approval unclear.

Julie Chen: Follow-up action items: Sam to notify customer of mitigation and ask to throttle large batch jobs; Ivan to keep watch and revert routing after 30m; Maya to propose tuning for admission control to better prioritize per-tenant SLAs (canary rule).

Sam Park: Notified customer, they confirmed acceptable. They also sent a repro script for the batch job:```#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":16}' &
done
wait
```They said it was an internal result-export job that accidentally targeted prod endpoint.

Maya Li: We should add a guard to block high-rate non-batched small requests: detect repeated short max_tokens=16 loops and treat as batch-like, then recommend using bulk/async API. Also update docs and send customer's SRE a best-practice note.

Ivan Petrov: Monitoring: I added an alert temporarily to notify if pool queue depth > 30 for > 2m and if autoscaler errors repeat. I also enabled a per-pool admission controller override for acme to keep their in-flight <= 24.

support-bot: Reminder: Create post-incident summary in #postmortems within 48h.

Julie Chen: I'll draft the postmortem, call out autoscaler quota failure, noisy neighbor batch, and admission controller tuning. Sam — please collect customer repro timeline and any logs they have.

Sam Park: Will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
